title: Security Audit Finding
description: A single candidate/confirmed/rejected security finding produced by an ai-security-audit run. Every confirmed finding must carry a complete threat model: who the attacker is, which boundary they cross, and the exact evidence chain.

id.description: Stable finding identifier, e.g. ASA-AUTHZ-001. The numeric suffix must be unique within a run for the same category.

title.description: One-line statement of the concrete weakness, not the category name.

confidence.description: How sure the hunter/validator is that the attack path is real, independent of severity.

path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path to the affected file. Must exist in the audited repository.

lines.description: Line or inclusive line range, e.g. '42' or '42-58'.

affected_components.description: Named routes, handlers, services, jobs, or modules involved.

attack_surface.description: The reachable entry point through which the attack begins (route, topic, bucket, CLI flag, CI event...).

attacker.description: Mandatory threat model: exactly who the attacker is, what they control, and what they are NOT (must state the trust position, e.g. 'an authenticated tenant user; they do not control the server process').

preconditions.description: Conditions that must hold for the attack path to work (deploy config, feature flags, privileges).

file.description: Repo-relative path if the evidence is file-backed (should exist).

detail.description: What the evidence shows and why it matters. Must be specific, not a restatement of the category.

data_flow.description: Ordered steps from attacker-controlled source to the vulnerable operation, e.g. ['POST /api/avatar body.filename (untrusted)', 'path.join(uploadsDir, filename) (no sanitization)', 'fs.createWriteStream -> arbitrary write inside process cwd'].

impact.description: Concrete worst-case outcome for the asset owner if exploited, tied to the detected application domain.

reproduction.description: Non-destructive steps a reviewer can follow (static reasoning, local test, or controlled PoC). Never include commands that attack third-party systems.

severity_reasoning.description: Why this severity given exploitability, privileges required, complexity, and C-I-A impact. Required for confirmed findings by mechanical validation policy, optional in schema.

validator.description: Identifier of the validating agent/session. Must differ from the discovering hunter when practical.

attempted_rejections.description: Disproof hypotheses the validator actually tested and why each failed to kill the finding.

reaudit.description: Populated by `security-audit reaudit` when comparing against a previous audit.
